note: Timor-Leste's banks are few: BNU Timor (Caixa Geral de Depósitos's bank, the largest issuer of cards), the state's BNCTL, Mandiri and BRI; only BNU's price list, which prices credit cards, was read. BNU Timor's price list (in force from 12 October 2026), in US dollars, read in full for its credit cards: the BNU VISA Classic and Gold cost 50 and 75 dollars a year, carry a fixed nominal rate of 20% a year, charge 2% for a cash advance (at least 5 dollars), and add a 3.5% surcharge on the exchange rate for every transaction in a currency other than the US dollar, written as the foreign spending share. A further 2% on payments at terminals outside the P24 network (which includes terminals abroad) has no separate form in the game and isn't added to it. The list's fees exclude any taxes, whose rate it doesn't state.
